public_rationale: The funding condition was not met. SoftBank reports completing a $22.5 billion investment in December 2025. That single payment exceeds the lower threshold in every completed post-publication twelve-month window available for assessment. Receiving funding neither proves nor disproves that OpenAI would fail without it.
limitations: The annual measurement window is an evaluator interpretation.
The financing basis is unspecified, which independently prevents a definitive money-based verdict.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If OpenAI does not receive $20-40 billion in funding a year, it will die.
conditions: if not fed $20-40 billion a year

statement.excerpt: Also, if it’s not fed $20 billion to $40 billion a year, it will die.

our_interpretation: OpenAI is the company identified by the surrounding paragraph.
Read 'fed' as receiving outside financing and 'die' as ceasing operations because it cannot finance them.
Use less than $20 billion, the bottom of the stated range, as the unambiguous funding shortfall.
Test completed twelve-month periods beginning on or after publication. The speaker did not specify calendar years or a delay between a funding shortfall and failure.
Continued operation while receiving substantial financing does not test this conditional claim.
criteria.support_condition: A documented financing shortfall below $20 billion over a completed twelve-month period is followed by OpenAI ceasing operations because it cannot finance them.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the financing shortfall occurs, reliable operating and financial records establish that OpenAI has become sustainably viable without the stated annual financing.

evidence.excerpt: the Company has fully satisfied its commitment to invest in OpenAI
evidence.locator: Opening paragraph, following the December 26 investment announcement
evidence.explanation: The paragraph reports a completed $22.5 billion investment on December 26. That payment alone exceeds $20 billion and falls within every completed twelve-month period beginning after publication and ending by the evaluation date; it contradicts the antecedent, not the predicted consequence.
